To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a two-stream neural architecture that facilitates information transfer between high-level holistic and local pixel features improves semantic segmentation performance, and b) this architecture can be trained with a single end-to-end optimization procedure.

1) a holistic analysis of the image is a valuable source of information that can help to improve pixel-level predictions in semantic segmentation; 2) this information can be effectively combined with local information by a neural network architecture that encourages information flow from the holistic stream to the local stream; 3) this architecture is particularly effective when the holistic and local streams share low-level features.
a two-stream neural architecture that facilitates information transfer from a holistic analysis branch to a semantic segmentation branch can outperform a single-stream architecture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of semantic segmentation, and we present a new network architecture that incorporates high-recall information from holistic analysis into the local pixel labeling task.
a novel approach to semantic segmentation that combines holistic and pixel-based reasoning to achieve state-of-the-art results.
how to best leverage holistic inference to facilitate semantic segmentation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our proposed method achieves the state-of-the-art results in semantic segmentation.

our method is the first to demonstrate the benefits of holistic reasoning for semantic segmentation, and the proposed two-stream architecture is an effective approach to integrating global and local information.
the proposed method is the best semantic segmentation approach to date, and that it will be a strong baseline for future research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a two-stream network architecture to facilitate holistic information flow to local pixel labeling.
we have developed a two-stream neural architecture to facilitate information flow from holistic image understanding to pixel-level semantic segmentation.
holistic information can help to improve the performance of semantic segmentation, especially when the training dataset is small and noisy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global information about image concepts provides valuable supervision for local semantic segmentation.

high-recall global inference of image concepts is an important source of information for semantic segmentation, and that a simple architecture that allows the information flow is sufficient to achieve state-of-the-art results.
